newsitem.title: JAPAN: Five years too short for Japan 'Big Bang' - Yamaichi.
newsitem.headline: Five years too short for Japan 'Big Bang' - Yamaichi.

text.p: The five-year time frame for Japan's financial "Big Bang" may be too short as Japan has been left behind by reforms in other centres, an executive of one of the nation's "Big Four" securities houses said on Friday.

"I don't think five years is very long for Japan to complete the reforms. Japanese reforms have been slower than Britain's 'Big Bang', so it would take longer," Takashi Kanasaki, a director of Yamaichi Securities Co Ltd, told the Foreign Correspondents' Club of Japan.

Earlier this month Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto unveiled plans for a five-year Big Bang to liberalise Japan's financial markets and catch up with reforms carried out more than a decade ago in Europe and North America.
Kanasaki also said: "If the government takes up broader reforms, including deregulation of the telecommunications industry and administrative restructuring, it would be a very big reform."
Asked if Japan could achieve such sweeping reforms, Kanasaki said: "I don't think Japan can do everything in five years."
Kanasaki said if the stock market had a clearer picture of details of the Big Bang, the Nikkei average would head above 23,000. The key stock index closed on Friday at 21,020.36.

He also said securities houses hoped the proposed liberalisation of stock brokerage commissions under the Big Bang would boost volume on the stock market to offset expected lower revenues from commissions in the future.
He also called for the abolition of a tax on securities transactions that he said had no equivalent in the United States or in Europe. -- Tokyo Equities Desk +81-3-3432-8027
